scimon.text: Which method can be used for the presence of ferromagnetic ground states, and why?

hidden_target.material_initial_state: As-cast high-entropy alloy FeCoNiTi (nominal 1:1:1:1) containing dual phases: fcc and hexagonal C14 Laves.
hidden_target.intervention: Rapid quenching (arc melting on water-cooled Cu hearth) to stabilize the dual-phase microstructure; synthesis of a compositionally matched C14-dominant variant (Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29) for comparison.
hidden_target.conditions: Magnetic measurements performed up to 400 K; electronic structure calculations for spin-polarized density of states.
hidden_target.structural_mediator: Coexistence of ferromagnetic fcc phase and C14 Laves phase, with specific chemical segregation (fcc: ~21.3Fe-24.8Co-32.2Ni-21.6Ti; C14: ~27.3Fe-26.6Co-17.4Ni-28.7Ti).
hidden_target.mechanism: Antiferromagnetic coupling between the Fe/Co/Ni sublattice and the Ti sublattice reduces saturation magnetization ($M_s$) but fosters a high-temperature ferromagnetic ordering in the fcc phase (1084 K). The orbital moment in the fcc phase, while small in isolation, contributes to coercivity in the presence of the C14 phase and spin-canted components, allowing domain wall pinning. The 214 K transition is attributed to the C14 phase, while 168 K and 1084 K transitions originate from the fcc phase.
hidden_target.predicted_outcome: The fcc phase in the dual-phase alloy will exhibit a coercive field significantly exceeding the 100 Oe limit of single-phase alloys, reaching approximately 667 Oe at 400 K, accompanied by multiple magnetic ordering temperatures distinct from the C14 phase.
hidden_target.baseline:
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni high-entropy alloys with $H_c 
gtr 100$ Oe and limited orbital moment contribution.
hidden_target.boundary: The mechanism relies on the specific dual-phase interface and the antiferromagnetic coupling; pure single-phase C14 or pure single-phase fcc variants do not exhibit the combined high $H_c$ and multi-transition behavior in the same manner.
hidden_target.discriminating_measurement: Synthesis of a C14-dominant alloy (Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29) to isolate C14-specific transitions (observed at ~246 K and 183 K) and compare magnetic behavior against the dual-phase FeCoNiTi to confirm the fcc phase is responsible for the 1084 K and 168 K transitions and the high coercivity.
hidden_target.actual_result: The as-cast FeCoNiTi alloy exhibited three ferromagnetic transitions (1084 K, 214 K, 168 K). The fcc phase was identified as the source of the high-temperature ordering (1084 K) and the 168 K transition, achieving a coercive field of 667 Oe at 400 K. Electronic structure calculations confirmed ferromagnetic ground states for both phases, with the fcc phase showing a spin-up/down density of states discrepancy at the Fermi level.
